## Overview

Models are often refinements of one another. A model may carry a label that
the dynamics never read: which introduction a case of a disease descends from,
or which of two colonies a live cell belongs to. Forgetting the label should
give the plainer model, run for run. This vignette makes that precise, as maps
between models, and checks it on CellularAutomataCore models.

A **map of models** `M → N` is a map `h` from the cell states of `M` to those
of `N`, applied cell by cell, with a map of parameters, that commutes with the
rules. That means the next state of `M`, mapped by `h`, is the next state of
`N` computed from the mapped cell and neighbours, for every local
configuration, with the same cell, time and seed. Then every run of `M`,
mapped by `h`, is the run of `N` from the mapped initial state. For stochastic
models this holds run by run, not only in distribution: both models draw the
same counter-based random numbers. Models and these maps form a category, and
moving models along maps of spaces is a functor on it.

This is a **research extension**, beyond the papers the package implements.
The Lean library in `proofs/` proves the laws (`ModelMap.run_map`, the
`Category` instance, `SpaceMap.pullFunctor`).

```{julia}
#| output: false
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using CategoricalCellularAutomata
using CellularAutomataCore: CellularAutomataCore, CAProblem, solve, Torus, VonNeumann,
                            Moore, @camodel, bernoulli, uniform
using Catlab: @relation, compose, id, dom, codom
using Plots
using Random
```

## The immigration game and Life

The immigration game is Life with two colours of live cells. A live cell
keeps its colour; a birth takes the colour that most of its three live
neighbours have. Births and deaths do not depend on the colours, so forgetting
them should give Life.

```{julia}
life = @camodel Life begin
    @states alive::Int = 0 ∈ (0, 1)
    @neighbourhood Moore(1)
    @rule begin
        n = sum(nbrs)
        cell == 1 ? Int(n == 2 || n == 3) : Int(n == 3)
    end
end
immigration = @camodel Immigration begin
    @states colour::Int = 0 ∈ (0, 1, 2)
    @neighbourhood Moore(1)
    @rule begin
        n = count(!=(0), nbrs)
        if cell != 0
            n == 2 || n == 3 ? cell : 0
        elseif n == 3
            count(==(1), nbrs) >= 2 ? 1 : 2
        else
            0
        end
    end
end
forget = ModelMap(immigration, life, c -> Int(c != 0))
```

`is_model_map` checks the commuting condition on every local configuration:
here all `3^9` patterns of a cell and its eight neighbours. Life's rule does
not read the cell context, so this check proves the map. Keeping only one
colour alive is not a map of models:

```{julia}
(forget=is_model_map(forget; contexts=1),
 one_colour=is_model_map(ModelMap(immigration, life, c -> Int(c == 1)); contexts=1))
```

`pushforward(f, prob)` maps a problem of the domain to one of the codomain,
from the mapped initial state. Its run is the original run with the colours
forgotten:

```{julia}
prob = CAProblem(immigration, (; colour=rand(Xoshiro(3), 0:2, 64, 48)), 40;
                 space=Torus(64, 48))
sol = solve(prob)
plain = solve(pushforward(forget, prob))
all(t -> pushforward(forget, sol.u[t]) == plain.u[t], eachindex(sol.u))
```

```{julia}
plot(heatmap(sol.u[end]'; c=cgrad([:white, :darkorange, :steelblue]; categorical=true),
             colorbar=false, clims=(0, 2), title="immigration game, step 40"),
     heatmap(plain.u[end]'; c=cgrad([:white, :black]; categorical=true), colorbar=false,
             clims=(0, 1), title="Life, step 40");
     layout=(1, 2), size=(800, 300), aspect_ratio=1, framestyle=:box, ticks=false,
     yflip=true, titlefontsize=10)
```

## Tracing introductions of a disease

A disease spreads through a field from three introductions. The plain model
is SIR on the von Neumann neighbourhood. The traced model also records, for
each case, the introduction it descends from. A newly infected cell takes the
label of one of its infected neighbours, chosen with a draw number of its own.
So the infection itself draws exactly as in the plain model, and the label
never feeds back on who is infected.

```{julia}
sir = @camodel SIR begin
    @states state::Symbol = :S ∈ (:S, :I, :R)
    @parameters β = 0.4 γ = 0.2
    @neighbourhood VonNeumann(1)
    @rule begin
        if cell == :S
            bernoulli(ctx, 1 - (1 - β)^count(==(:I), nbrs), 1) ? :I : :S
        elseif cell == :I
            bernoulli(ctx, γ, 2) ? :R : :I
        else
            cell
        end
    end
end
traced = @camodel TracedSIR begin
    @states state::Symbol = :S ∈ (:S, :I, :R) lineage::Int = 0 ∈ 0:3
    @parameters β = 0.4 γ = 0.2
    @neighbourhood VonNeumann(1)
    @rule begin
        if cell.state == :S
            k = count(n -> n.state == :I, nbrs)
            if bernoulli(ctx, 1 - (1 - β)^k, 1)
                j = clamp(ceil(Int, uniform(ctx, 3) * k), 1, k)
                source = nbrs[findall(n -> n.state == :I, collect(nbrs))[j]]
                (state=:I, lineage=source.lineage)
            else
                cell
            end
        elseif cell.state == :I
            bernoulli(ctx, γ, 2) ? (state=:R, lineage=cell.lineage) : cell
        else
            cell
        end
    end
end
untrace = ModelMap(traced, sir, c -> c.state)
is_model_map(untrace)
```

The check covers every pattern of states and labels in a cell and its four
neighbours, at eight cell contexts. Each context draws different random
numbers, and both models must agree at each one. For a stochastic rule this
samples the random numbers rather than proving the map; here the map holds
for all of them, because both models read draws 1 and 2 in the same way. The
traced run, with its labels forgotten, is the plain run from the same
introductions, at every step:

```{julia}
ports = Dict(CartesianIndex(10, 12) => 1, CartesianIndex(50, 18) => 2,
             CartesianIndex(30, 50) => 3)
start = (; state=I -> haskey(ports, I) ? :I : :S, lineage=I -> get(ports, I, 0))
prob = CAProblem(traced, start, 80, (; β=0.45); space=Torus(60, 60), seed=4)
sol = solve(prob)
plain = solve(pushforward(untrace, prob))
all(t -> pushforward(untrace, sol.u[t]) == plain.u[t], eachindex(sol.u))
```

Part way through the epidemic, the labels show where each introduction's
descendants have gone (grey: not yet infected), while the plain model shows
only who is susceptible, infected or recovered:

```{julia}
labels(u) = map((s, l) -> s == :S ? 0 : l, u.state, u.lineage)
code(u) = map(s -> s == :S ? 0 : s == :I ? 2 : 1, u)
snapshot = 26 # step 25
plot(heatmap(labels(sol.u[snapshot])';
             c=cgrad([:lightgrey, :firebrick, :seagreen, :royalblue]; categorical=true),
             colorbar=false, clims=(0, 3), title="traced: introductions 1, 2, 3"),
     heatmap(code(plain.u[snapshot])'; c=:viridis, colorbar=false, clims=(0, 2),
             title="plain SIR (purple S, green R, yellow I)");
     layout=(1, 2), size=(800, 400), aspect_ratio=1, framestyle=:box, ticks=false,
     yflip=true, titlefontsize=10)
```

## When a label feeds back

If one introduction is a more transmissible strain, its label changes who
gets infected, and forgetting it is no longer a map of models. The check fails
on some local configuration, and the runs part. Both epidemics eventually reach
almost every cell of the torus, so the difference shows in the timing:

```{julia}
virulent = @camodel VirulentSIR begin
    @states state::Symbol = :S ∈ (:S, :I, :R) lineage::Int = 0 ∈ 0:3
    @parameters β = 0.4 γ = 0.2
    @neighbourhood VonNeumann(1)
    @rule begin
        if cell.state == :S
            escape = prod((n.state == :I ? (n.lineage == 3 ? 0.2 : 1 - β) : 1.0
                           for n in nbrs); init=1.0)
            k = count(n -> n.state == :I, nbrs)
            if bernoulli(ctx, 1 - escape, 1)
                j = clamp(ceil(Int, uniform(ctx, 3) * k), 1, k)
                source = nbrs[findall(n -> n.state == :I, collect(nbrs))[j]]
                (state=:I, lineage=source.lineage)
            else
                cell
            end
        elseif cell.state == :I
            bernoulli(ctx, γ, 2) ? (state=:R, lineage=cell.lineage) : cell
        else
            cell
        end
    end
end
drop = ModelMap(virulent, sir, c -> c.state)
vprob = CAProblem(virulent, start, 80, (; β=0.45); space=Torus(60, 60), seed=4)
vsol, vplain = solve(vprob), solve(pushforward(drop, vprob))
reached(u) = count(!=(:S), u)
(is_model_map=is_model_map(drop),
 first_step_that_differs=findfirst(t -> pushforward(drop, vsol.u[t]) != vplain.u[t],
                                   eachindex(vsol.u)) - 1,
 reached_at_step_25_with_the_strain=reached(vsol.u[26].state),
 reached_at_step_25_label_forgotten=reached(vplain.u[26]))
```

## A category of models

Maps of models compose: cell states and parameters go through both maps. With
identities, CellularAutomataCore models and their maps form a category, an
instance of Catlab's `ThCategory`. Merging introduction 3 into introduction 2
is a map from the traced model to itself, and following it by forgetting the
labels is again a map of models, the same as forgetting them directly:

```{julia}
merge3 = ModelMap(traced, traced, c -> (state=c.state, lineage=min(c.lineage, 2)))
both = compose(merge3, untrace)
(merge_is_a_map=is_model_map(merge3), composite_is_a_map=is_model_map(both),
 domain=dom(both).name, codomain=codom(both).name,
 same_as_forgetting=all(u -> pushforward(both, u) == pushforward(untrace, u), sol.u),
 identity=all(u -> pushforward(compose(id(traced), untrace), u) ==
                   pushforward(untrace, u), sol.u))
```

## Parameters, and composites

A map of models also maps parameters. A composite built with `oapply` keeps
each box's parameters under the box's name. Projecting a composite of SIR and
a box that counts each cell's days infected onto SIR maps the composite's
parameters to `p.sir`. It is a map of models when the boxes share random
numbers. Otherwise the SIR box draws from a seed of its own, and the
projection fails:

```{julia}
counter = @camodel Counter begin
    @states state::Symbol = :S ∈ (:S, :I, :R) days::Int = 0
    @neighbourhood VonNeumann(1)
    @rule (state=cell.state, days=cell.days + (cell.state == :I))
end
d = @relation (state,) begin
    sir(state)
    counter(state)
end
boxes = (sir=OpenCAModel(sir), counter=OpenCAModel(counter; ports=[:state], reads=[:state]))
map([true, false]) do shared
    comp = oapply(d, boxes; shared_randomness=shared)
    proj = ModelMap(comp, sir, c -> c.state; parameters=p -> p.sir)
    cells = [(state=s, counter_days=n) for s in (:S, :I, :R) for n in 0:2]
    cprob = CAProblem(comp, (; state=start.state), 60,
                      (; sir=(β=0.45, γ=0.2), counter=(;)); space=Torus(60, 60), seed=4)
    csol = solve(cprob)
    psol = solve(pushforward(proj, cprob))
    (shared_randomness=shared, is_model_map=is_model_map(proj; cells),
     runs_agree=all(t -> pushforward(proj, csol.u[t]) == psol.u[t], eachindex(csol.u)))
end
```

The `days` layer has no finite domain, so the check is given the cell values
to try with `cells`.

## Maps of models and maps of spaces

Moving a problem along a map of spaces (the vignette on geometries)
and pushing it along a map of models commute: moving the traced problem from
a 20 × 20 torus to the 60 × 60 torus that covers it and then forgetting the
labels gives the same problem, and the same run, as forgetting first and then
moving. Moving models along a map of spaces is a functor between the
categories of models on the two spaces.

```{julia}
φ = covering(Torus(60, 60), Torus(20, 20), VonNeumann(1))
small = CAProblem(traced, (; state=I -> I == CartesianIndex(5, 5) ? :I : :S,
                          lineage=I -> Int(I == CartesianIndex(5, 5))), 30;
                  space=Torus(20, 20), seed=2)
one = pushforward(untrace, pullback(φ, small; space=Torus(60, 60)))
two = pullback(φ, pushforward(untrace, small); space=Torus(60, 60))
solve(one).u == solve(two).u
```

## Summary

| map | from | to | a map of models? |
|---|---|---|---|
| forget colours | immigration game | Life | yes: proved by checking every pattern |
| forget lineages | traced SIR | SIR | yes, run by run with shared random numbers |
| forget lineages | SIR with a more transmissible lineage | SIR | no: the label feeds back |
| merge lineages 3 and 2 | traced SIR | itself | yes; composes with forgetting |
| project onto a box | `oapply` composite | the box's model | yes when the boxes share random numbers, with parameters `p -> p.sir` |

A map of models says when a richer model contains a plainer one exactly, so
the plainer model's results hold for the richer one, run by run, and the
labels it carries can be read off for free. Together with maps of spaces, it
moves a model to a new space and to a coarser description in either order.
